c.tagline: Aegean gateway of seafront promenades, seafood and easy sunshine.

taxi.fareNote: Taxis are metered; book through the BiTaksi or municipal iTaksi apps, and Uber in İzmir dispatches licensed taxis rather than private cars.

emergency.note: 112 is Türkiye's unified emergency number for police, ambulance, and fire.

avoid.reason: Pickpocketing around Konak/Kemeraltı bazaar and the seafront

hood_desc: İzmir's lively, bohemian heart in the Konak district, lined with restaurants, bars, boutiques and the palm-fringed Kordon seafront promenade that fills with outdoor cafes at sunset; best for young travelers who want nightlife and dining within walking distance.

The historic and commercial center around the Clock Tower (Saat Kulesi), the sprawling Kemeraltı Bazaar and the ancient Agora; the main transport hub with metro, tram, ferry and bus links, ideal for first-timers who want everything walkable.

A relaxed, upscale seaside district across the bay from Konak with a long waterfront, parks, shopping and a laid-back local feel; superbly linked by ferry, train and tram and popular with families wanting calm and sea views.

A leafy district on the eastern side of the city home to Ege University and a large student population, with lively cafes, budget eats and green campus grounds; suits younger travelers and those wanting an authentic, affordable base.

A coastal suburban stretch southwest of the center known for the Balçova thermal springs, the Balçova teleferik (cable car), marinas and quiet residential seafront living; suits travelers wanting a calm, scenic base away from the crowds.
lodging: Wyndham Grand Izmir Ozdilek Thermal & Spa

water.note: Tap water is chlorinated but most locals drink bottled; bottled is the safer choice.

transit.hours: The Metro runs roughly 06:00 to 00:20 with trains about every 5 minutes; trams, İZBAN and ferries run daytime to late evening, with ESHOT night buses covering the overnight gap.
transit.note: İzmir's transport wraps around the bay: a single Metro line plus three tram lines (Konak, Karşıyaka and Buca), the İZBAN suburban railway spanning Aliağa to the airport, an extensive ESHOT bus network, and İZDENİZ passenger ferries that cross the harbour between Konak, Karşıyaka, Bostanlı and other quays.
transit.pay: Tap a single rechargeable İzmirimKart across the Metro, trams, İZBAN, ferries and buses, with cheap transfers between them; buy and top up cards at station machines and kiosks. Single rides cost well under US$1 with the card.

transit.m: İZBAN suburban train to Alsancak / city center (~30-40 min, every 10-20 min)
Havaş / ESHOT airport bus to the center (~40 min)

tip.r: Not obligatory; rounding up the bill or leaving 5-10% at restaurants for good service is appreciated but not expected.

food.name: Boyoz
food.desc: A coiled, flaky Sephardic pastry brought by Spanish Jews in the 1490s and now made nowhere else in Turkiye. Eaten warm with a hard-boiled egg.

places.name: Dostlar Firini
places.note: Old bakery in the historic Jewish quarter; locals queue from early morning for trays straight out of the oven.

places.name: Kemeralti Bazaar bakeries
places.note: Several boyoz counters along Anafartalar Caddesi sell them by the piece with tea.

places.name: Boyozcu Ferit
places.note: Long-running boyoz stall near the Kordon; classic plain and cheese versions.

food.name: Kumru
food.desc: Izmir's sandwich, built on crisp sesame gevrek bread and stacked with griddled kasar cheese, sucuk, tomato and pickled pepper.

places.name: Kardesler Bufe
places.note: One of the safest bets in town for a classic hot kumru, open late.

places.name: Zeynel Ergin Gevrek Firini
places.note: The name locals give first for proper gevrek and the cold kumru.

places.name: Kumrucu Sevki
places.note: Cesme-born kumru chain with Izmir branches; generous cheese and sucuk.

food.name: Sogus
food.desc: A cold Izmir street classic: paper-thin slices of offal and tongue chopped with tomato, onion, parsley and cumin, rolled into flatbread.

places.name: Kemeralti Bazaar sogus stalls
places.note: The bazaar's back lanes are the traditional home of sogus; the busy carts turn over fastest.

places.name: Anafartalar Caddesi carts
places.note: Cluster of veteran sogus sellers working the bazaar's main artery at lunchtime.

places.name: Bostanli market street
places.note: Ferry-side stalls on the north shore where locals grab sogus after the crossing.

food.name: Midye dolma
food.desc: Black mussels stuffed with spiced pilaf, currants and pine nuts, served open by the dozen and eaten with a squeeze of lemon.

places.name: Demirkaya Midye Dolma
places.note: Opposite the Alsancak ferry pier, serving stuffed mussels hot around the clock.

places.name: Kordon seafront carts
places.note: Evening mussel carts along the promenade; pick the one with the longest line.

places.name: Bostanli Iskele stalls
places.note: Sunset spot where mussel sellers set up beside the ferry terminal.

food.name: Aegean herb mezes
food.desc: Izmir's meyhane spread of wild greens: sea beans, radika, arapsaci and hibes, dressed in olive oil and lemon and eaten before the fish.

places.name: Deniz Restaurant
places.note: Kordon institution inside the Izmir Palas hotel, famous for its meze trolley and fish.

places.name: Topcu'nun Yeri
places.note: Decades-old Izmir kitchen serving classic Aegean mezes alongside keskek and kebabs.

places.name: Veli Usta Balik
places.note: Reliable seafront fish house where the herb mezes arrive by the tray.

food.name: Sambali
food.desc: A dense semolina cake soaked in syrup, cut into diamonds and sold by the slice from bazaar carts. Izmir's cheapest and most nostalgic sweet.

places.name: Kemeralti Bazaar sweet carts
places.note: Sambali trays sold by the slice all through the covered bazaar.

places.name: Kadifekale road stalls
places.note: Traditional sellers on the way up to the castle, best in the afternoon.

places.name: Karsiyaka Carsi
places.note: North-shore shopping street with several long-standing sambali and lokma sellers.

food.name: Raki
food.desc: Anise spirit clouded white with water, the compulsory partner to a table of Aegean mezes and grilled fish. Sipped slowly, never rushed.

places.name: Deniz Restaurant
places.note: Classic Kordon setting for a long raki dinner over seafood.

places.name: Alsancak meyhanes
places.note: The lanes behind the Kordon are wall-to-wall taverns with live fasil music.

places.name: Foca waterfront tavernas
places.note: Hour from the centre; harbourside raki tables that locals drive out for.

food.name: Urla wine
food.desc: The peninsula west of Izmir has revived an ancient wine route, with bottles from native Bornova Misketi and Urla Karasi grapes.

places.name: Urla Sarapcilik
places.note: Flagship winery on the Urla route with tastings and a vineyard restaurant.

places.name: USCA Winery
places.note: Boutique producer known for reviving indigenous Aegean grape varieties.

places.name: Alsancak wine bars
places.note: City-centre bars pour Urla and Bozcaada bottles by the glass.

landmarks: İzmir Clock Tower (Saat Kulesi)
This ornate Ottoman-era clock tower anchors bustling Konak Square and has become the unofficial symbol of the city. Its intricate stonework glows beautifully at dusk.
Kadifekale (Velvet Castle)
Perched atop a hill overlooking the city, this ancient hilltop fortress dates back to the Hellenistic era. The sunset views over İzmir's bay from up here are absolutely stunning.
Ancient Agora of Smyrna
Wander among the columns and arches of this remarkably preserved Roman marketplace, once the commercial heart of ancient Smyrna. It's a fascinating open-air journey into antiquity.
Kordon (Kordonboyu Waterfront)
This lively seaside promenade along the Gulf of İzmir is where locals jog, cycle, and sip tea at sunset cafés. It offers gorgeous views back toward the Clock Tower and hills beyond.
Kemeraltı Bazaar
Lose yourself in this sprawling historic market of narrow alleys, spice stalls, and centuries-old mosques and synagogues. It's a sensory feast of colors, aromas, and everyday Turkish life.
Konak Pier
Designed by Gustave Eiffel, this iron-framed waterfront building now houses shops and cafés with a striking industrial silhouette. It's a favorite spot for a coastal photo with a touch of history.
Asansör (The Elevator)

This charming 1907 historic elevator lifts visitors up a steep hillside in the Jewish quarter of Karataş, saving a long climb. The rooftop café at the top offers one of the best panoramic views of the bay.
İzmir Archaeology Museum

This museum showcases treasures unearthed from the region's ancient civilizations, including statues, sarcophagi, and coins spanning thousands of years. It's a rich complement to a visit to the nearby Agora.
Bostanlı Sunset Point

On the Karşıyaka side of the bay, this relaxed waterfront spot delivers arguably the most breathtaking sunset views in İzmir, framed by sailboats and the distant city skyline. It's a beloved gathering place for locals at golden hour.
Kültürpark
A sprawling 420,000-square-meter city park built over the ruins of the 1922 Great Fire of Smyrna, home to the annual İzmir International Fair and a history museum.

train.note: No international trains. İzmir Basmane is the station for long-distance services, with the overnight Izmir Blue Train to Ankara and the Konya Mavi Treni, plus regional trains east to Denizli for Pamukkale and south toward Selçuk for Ephesus. Alsancak station handles some services and the İZBAN suburban network links both to the airport. Book on TCDD e-bilet from 15 days out.

bus.note: International coaches to Europe generally start in Istanbul rather than İzmir. The huge İzmir Otogar north-east of the centre is a domestic hub, with Kamil Koç (https://www.kamilkoc.com.tr/), Metro Turizm (https://www.metroturizm.com.tr/en) and Pamukkale (https://www.pamukkale.com.tr/) running to Istanbul (about 8 hours), Bodrum, Antalya and Cappadocia. Book through obilet (https://www.obilet.com/en/).

intl.to: Chios (Greece) - sails from Çeşme, ~1 hr west of İzmir
Karşıyaka, Bostanlı, Alsancak & Konak (Türkiye) - across the bay

ferry.note: The international crossing to the Greek island of Chios does not leave from İzmir itself but from Çeşme, about an hour west by road, and runs mainly from spring to autumn - bring your passport and check Greek entry rules. Within the city, İZDENİZ ferries criss-cross the Gulf of İzmir on ordinary transit fares and are the pleasantest way between Konak and Karşıyaka.

full.name: Ephesus Ancient City
full.blurb: A short drive from İzmir, this UNESCO World Heritage site boasts the breathtaking Library of Celsus and one of the best-preserved ancient cities in the Mediterranean. It's an essential bucket-list stop for history lovers.
